items.hook: The number of uses needed to learn an unknown quantum process is now pinned down, with a matching lower bound.
items.hook_turn: with a matching lower bound.
items.summary: The authors settle how many queries to a quantum channel are needed to learn it to fixed accuracy in diamond distance, giving an algorithm and a matching lower bound. The method reduces channel learning to pure-state tomography of the Choi state. The optimality holds at constant accuracy, so scaling in the precision is not covered.
items.title: Optimal learning of quantum channels in diamond distance

items.hook: Gut microbiome diversity at engraftment did not predict non-relapse death after stem cell transplant.
items.hook_turn: did not predict non-relapse death after stem cell transplant.
items.summary: In 304 transplant recipients with 2575 stool samples, microbiome diversity at engraftment was unrelated to non-relapse mortality, missing the primary endpoint. Lower baseline diversity did go with shorter survival, and post-transplant cyclophosphamide lowered diversity versus tacrolimus and methotrexate in exploratory analyses. Those secondary findings are associations, not shown causes.
items.title: Effect of two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens on the gut microbiome in a randomized phase 3 trial.

items.hook: A 46.5-million-cell atlas across 160 diseases reveals shared cell-response patterns across organs.
items.hook_turn: reveals shared cell-response patterns across organs.
items.summary: PANGEA remaps public single-cell data with an automated pipeline and a 32-type, 165-subtype cell classification, then compares disease responses across 48 organs. It finds recurring disease archetypes and works as a reference for spatial transcriptomics. It rests on public datasets of uneven quality, so batch and sampling biases may remain.
items.title: PANGEA: an integrated cell atlas across diverse biological contexts enables systematic profiling of multicellular responses in human diseases.

items.hook: A genetic study of over 1.2 million people finds 343 pain-linked regions, 92 of them new.
items.hook_turn: 92 of them new.
items.summary: Meta-analysis of three biobanks covering 1,235,695 European-ancestry people found 343 independent loci for multidimensional pain, plus sex-specific loci and 490 prioritized genes. Mendelian randomization suggested causal links to psychiatric and substance use disorders and C-reactive protein. The data are European-ancestry only and the female sample is much smaller than the male one.
items.title: Gene discovery and pleiotropic architecture of multidimensional pain in a genome-wide association study of >1.2 million individuals.

items.hook: Magnetic particle imaging spots early brain bleeding in injured mice that MRI misses at 24 hours.
items.hook_turn: that MRI misses at 24 hours.
items.summary: Mice with a moderate closed-head injury received iron oxide nanoparticles, and magnetic particle imaging showed strong local signal at the impact site that faded by 7 days. Sham animals showed none, and only this method clearly marked the injury at 24 hours versus MRI. It is a mouse study of one injury model, so human diagnostic value is unproven.
items.title: Sensitive detection of in vivo traumatic brain injury foci using magnetic particle imaging.

items.hook: Two quantum observers can be certain they disagree, but only when their measurements do not commute.
items.hook_turn: but only when their measurements do not commute.
items.summary: The paper proves a quantum version of Aumann's Agreement Theorem: if the observers' measurements commute with each other and the property, common certainty forces equal probabilities. A qutrit-qubit-qubit model breaks this with common certainty of disagreement, and storing outcomes in a classical register restores agreement. The results are for finite-dimensional, projective-measurement setups.
items.title: The quantum agreement theorem.
items.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.hook: A p38α-MK2 kinase pathway builds nuclear actin after chemo; blocking it sensitizes ovarian cancer cells.
items.hook_turn: blocking it sensitizes ovarian cancer cells.
items.summary: A deep learning tool, nFANet, counted nuclear F-actin and a kinome screen identified p38α MAPK as a regulator that acts through MK2 and formins. Inhibiting or knocking out the pathway made ovarian cancer cells more sensitive to platinum therapy. The work is in cell lines and models, so patient benefit is not shown.
items.title: The p38α MAPK-MK2 axis drives chemotherapy-mediated nuclear actin remodeling to promote ovarian cancer progression.
items.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.hook: Excess luminophore lets light-emission microscopy image depth, revealing 3D shape of algae and spheroids.
items.hook_turn: revealing 3D shape of algae and spheroids.
items.summary: Raising the ruthenium luminophore to coreactant ratio lets the glowing layer drift away from the electrode over time, and objects that block this light reveal their depth. Simulations and scanning electrochemical microscopy back the diffusion picture, and spirulina and cell spheroids served as demos. Only insulating micro-to-mesoscale objects were tested.
items.title: Diffusional depth profiling using electrochemiluminescence microscopy.
items.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.hook: A brain receptor needs a second, always-on receptor to signal and ease psychosis-like signs in mice.
items.hook_turn: and ease psychosis-like signs in mice.
items.summary: Mouse hippocampal neurons let the mGlu2 receptor trigger calcium signals only when the platelet-activating factor receptor, which is constitutively active, is also present. Blocking that partner receptor weakened the signal, and the partnership was needed for mGlu2 drugs to rescue cognition and behavior in a mouse model of NMDA receptor hypofunction. The evidence is from mice and cultured neurons, so human benefit is untested.
items.title: Synergy between Gq and Gi proteins for the antipsychotic-like effects of mGlu2 receptors.
items.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.hook: Graphene's electrons flow like a fluid, and a new device measures their viscosity directly.
items.hook_turn: and a new device measures their viscosity directly.
items.summary: Corbino-shaped graphene devices let magnetoresistance separate ohmic resistance from viscous flow in the same sample. In monolayer and bilayer graphene the electron-electron scattering rate rises linearly with temperature, not as T squared as in ordinary metals, matching a predicted tomographic fluid regime. The match to theory is consistent with, not proof of, that regime, and only graphene was tested.
items.title: Quantitative measurement of viscosity in two-dimensional electron fluids.

items.hook: Webb finds carbon dioxide ice mixed into water ice around the young star beta Pictoris.

readout.label: Crystallinity of water ice in disk

items.summary: Near-infrared spectra of the disk show amorphous water ice and CO2 ice, including the rare 13CO2 form, mixed at about 1 CO2 to 10 water. That mix suggests the ices formed in cold conditions, likely in interstellar space, and that frequent collisions spread icy grains through the disk. The conclusions rest on spectral modeling of one disk.
items.title: Carbon dioxide and amorphous water ices in the debris disk around β Pictoris.

items.hook: Boosting helper T cells before they reach the tumor made immunotherapy work better in colorectal cancer mice.
items.hook_turn: before they reach the tumor made immunotherapy work better in colorectal cancer mice.
items.summary: Imaging of patient tumors showed helper-T-cell-rich immune neighborhoods in tumors that respond to anti-PD-1 therapy, but not in those that resist it. In mouse models of resistant tumors, adding an OX40 agonist to PD-1 blockade expanded early helper T cells in lymph nodes and slowed tumor growth. The therapeutic effect was shown only in mice.
items.title: Differentiation of stem-like CD4+ T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer.

items.hook: Squeezing twisted graphene changes its electrical resistance over 100 times more than ordinary metals.
items.hook_turn: changes its electrical resistance over 100 times more than ordinary metals.
items.summary: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene under continuous uniaxial strain showed a very large resistance response, with a gauge factor over two orders of magnitude above conventional metals. In some doping ranges the response grew in a Curie-Weiss-like way as temperature fell, hinting at nematic or fluctuating-moment physics. The origin is discussed, not established.
items.title: Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene.

items.hook: A root-inspired microneedle adhesive joined tiny blood vessels in rats 78% faster than suturing.
items.hook_turn: joined tiny blood vessels in rats 78% faster than suturing.

readout.label: Shorter procedure time in rat models

items.summary: The adhesive pairs a water-repelling polymer with tetrahedral microneedles that interlock with vessel walls, and carries a wireless sensor with AI to track blood flow and graft health. In rats it cut procedure time and reduced thickening of the vessel lining. Results are from rat models only.
items.title: AI-monitored bioadhesive for sutureless microvascular anastomosis.

items.hook: Atmospheric oxygen data show the ocean carbon sink grew since 1990 while the land sink did not.
items.hook_turn: while the land sink did not.

readout.label: Ocean carbon sink growth per decade

items.summary: Thirty years of atmospheric O2 and CO2 measurements were used to separate ocean and land uptake of fossil carbon. The ocean sink grew and took up 35% of emissions over 1990 to 2019, while the net land sink showed no robust trend. This conflicts with many process-based models, though the land estimate carries a large uncertainty of 0.5 Pg C per year.
items.title: Atmospheric O2 reveals a strengthening ocean carbon sink and a stagnant net land sink since 1990.

items.hook: Genes can predict which way fly color evolves, but not which genes will do the changing.
items.hook_turn: but not which genes will do the changing.
items.summary: Fruit fly populations evolved in outdoor mesocosms and in the lab while the team tracked allele frequencies and pigmentation. A genotype-phenotype map stayed stable across populations and correctly gave the direction of change, yet the specific responding loci were largely unpredictable. The finding concerns one trait in one species.
items.title: Limited genomic predictability of complex trait evolution despite genotype-phenotype stability.

items.hook: An immune receptor's TIR domain makes a molecule and keeps it as glue to assemble its signaling complex.
items.hook_turn: and keeps it as glue to assemble its signaling complex.
items.summary: The TLR4 TIR domain turns out to be an enzyme that breaks down NAD+ once, when allosterically activated. The product, ADP-ribose, stays trapped and helps bind the adaptor TIRAP into a complex that starts signaling. This changes the view of animal TIR domains as passive scaffolds, though the work is biochemical and structural rather than in whole animals.
items.title: A trapped catalytic product acts as molecular glue for innate immune signalosome assembly.

items.hook: A map of 854,911 cells shows how the tissue around early breast cancer changes before it turns invasive.
items.hook_turn: before it turns invasive.
items.summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing of fresh samples from 159 patients, plus spatial transcriptomics on 39 samples, covered normal breast, DCIS and invasive cancer. Fibroblasts, vascular cells and basal cells remodel around DCIS, and many changes persist into invasive disease. It covers estrogen-receptor positive DCIS only and describes changes, not causes.
items.title: A cellular atlas of the preinvasive breast cancer microenvironment.

items.hook: Wild elephant social networks split into smaller, isolated groups after years of gradual member turnover.
items.hook_turn: after years of gradual member turnover.
items.summary: Tracking 443 wild female Asian elephants for 12 years, researchers watched networks fracture once turnover accumulated. Ties changed both from lost members and from shifting bonds among those who stayed. The data come from one population in one region, so how general the tipping behavior is remains open.
items.title: Increased demographic turnover and isolation precede social fragmentation in Asian elephants.

items.hook: Seafloor landslides were caught on camera creeping slowly uphill, not collapsing all at once.
items.hook_turn: not collapsing all at once.
items.summary: This is the first direct monitoring of fully submarine landslides in nature, at the Homathko Delta in Canada. They retreated slowly upslope, the signature of breaching, and fed long-lasting turbidity currents that carry sediment and carbon offshore. Longer-lasting loads matter for seabed structures. The observations come from a single delta.
items.title: Direct monitoring of breaching in deltaic submarine landslides.

items.hook: A 125,000-year-old Arabian lakeshore site holds stone points with poison residue from hunting.
items.hook_turn: with poison residue from hunting.

readout.label: Approximate age of the Arabian site

items.summary: At 'Uruq Aljelibah in Saudi Arabia, stone tools show use-wear, impact damage and residues of a poisonous plant, Acokanthera schimperi, alongside bones of hippo, buffalo, camel and other large animals. This suggests hafted, poisoned weapons and plant processing by early humans on a green Arabia. The tool makers are not identified from fossils, and one site cannot show how widespread the practice was.
items.title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore.

items.hook: Dry climates push river nitrate up worldwide, creating pollution hotspots far from farms and cities.
items.hook_turn: creating pollution hotspots far from farms and cities.

readout.label: People living where nitrate exceeds ecological limit

items.summary: Machine-learning maps covering about 2.9 million river segments show aridity raising nitrate across land uses. Concentrations exceed ecological thresholds on about 33% of land, and health thresholds on 2%. Because the maps are modeled rather than measured everywhere, local values may differ, and the aridity link is statistical.
items.title: Climate aridity amplifies global riverine nitrate beyond human inputs.

items.hook: An atlas of 667 dog tumors lists 39 cancer drivers and compares them with human cancers.

readout.label: Canine tumor-normal pairs in the atlas

items.summary: Researchers built an open database of whole-exome data from 667 dog tumor and normal pairs across 10 cancer types, with a shared pipeline for variant calling. Selection analysis found 39 driver genes, and comparison with human cancers showed both shared and dog-specific mechanisms. It is a resource more than a single discovery, and the less-sampled tumor types support only descriptive conclusions.
items.title: The genetic landscape of canine tumors: Insights from the Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA).

items.hook: Lysosomes refill their calcium through TMEM184 proteins, a long-missing transporter.
items.hook_turn: a long-missing transporter.
items.summary: A genetic screen of lysosomal membrane proteins found that TMEM184 proteins carry calcium into lysosomes, the uptake step that was previously unidentified. Losing TMEM184B and C emptied calcium stores and disrupted membrane repair and related functions, and a human mutation linked to a neurodevelopmental disorder impaired transport. Mice lacking Tmem184b had severe motor problems. The work is in cells and mice, so its relevance to human disease is inferred from one mutation.
items.title: TMEM184 proteins are Ca2+ uptake transporters in lysosomes.

items.hook: A 3D mantle model with a weak asthenosphere explains West Antarctica's uplift and gravity change.
items.summary: Ice loss in West Antarctica has lifted the bedrock and lowered gravity. The authors built rebound models with a three-dimensional, temperature-dependent mantle and an ice history from 1900 to 2020, and matched both GPS crustal motion and GRACE satellite gravity data. The same weak-asthenosphere mantle also fits million-year convection, but the ice history is a reconstruction and not a measurement.
items.title: Geodetic observations in West Antarctica reveal geodynamically consistent 3D mantle viscosity.

items.hook: Andes hantavirus genomes from a cruise ship outbreak point to person-to-person spread onboard.

readout.label: Identified cases in the cruise ship outbreak

items.summary: An international team sequenced Andes virus from 10 of 13 cases in an April 2026 cruise ship outbreak. Genomes, symptom onset dates, and contact patterns fit one or very few spillovers before boarding, followed by spread between passengers. The virus is not an unusual strain. Three cases had no sequence, and the origin of the spillover is not identified here.
items.title: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome outbreak linked to cruise ship travel in April-May 2026.

items.hook: An Andes virus lineage circulated in Patagonia 2018 to 2025; the cruise ship source stays unknown.
items.hook_turn: the cruise ship source stays unknown.
items.summary: Comparing genomes tied the 2026 cruise ship outbreak to a 2018 outbreak in Argentina and to a single Andes virus lineage seen in northern Patagonia through 2025. The 2018 outbreak may also have involved person-to-person spread, but there was no sign of widespread community transmission. Travel routes of the first cases did not fit the expected incubation period, so the actual source remains unresolved.
items.title: Long-term local circulation of an Andes virus lineage in northern Patagonia is linked to the M/V Hondius outbreak.

items.hook: Human movement drove early spread of the 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak, doubling about every 10 days.
items.hook_turn: doubling about every 10 days.
items.summary: Researchers combined case and testing records from Ituri province, DR Congo, with human mobility data to study the first weeks of a Bundibugyo virus outbreak. Between May 10 and June 1, affected health zones rose by 12 and health areas by 49, with movement as a main driver of the spread. The estimate covers only the early phase and depends on how complete early detection was.
items.title: Early epidemiological and spatial assessment of the Bundibugyo virus outbreak 2026.

items.hook: Clumps of ESCRT-0 protein bud vesicles off cilia without the usual ESCRT-III machinery.
items.hook_turn: without the usual ESCRT-III machinery.
items.summary: Cilia release small vesicles that carry the Hedgehog receptor SMO, and this work shows that ESCRT-0 condenses at the ciliary tip and clusters ubiquitinated SMO to make them bud. Blocking condensation stopped SMO release, and forcing ESCRT-0 together with light-controlled SMO clustering rebuilt budding. The experiments were done in mouse kidney cells, so other cell types are untested.
items.title: ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering drive extracellular vesicle budding from cilia.

items.hook: New observations suggest the ocean absorbs more carbon and land absorbs less.
items.summary: This perspective covers new observations, tied to atmospheric oxygen by its title, which suggest the ocean takes up more carbon than assumed and land takes up less. The abstract does not describe the method or give numbers. It is commentary on another study, so the result is only as strong as that study.
items.title: Oxygen tells the tale of Earth's carbon sinks.

items.hook: Heat from thermogenic plants serves as a signal to pollinating beetles.
items.summary: This perspective describes work indicating that beetles detect the infrared heat given off by thermogenic plants and use it as a pollination cue. The abstract gives no experimental details. As commentary, it depends on the original study for its evidence.
items.title: Thermal infrared pollination by beetles.

items.hook: A gene therapy let a drug quiet brain cells and reduce seizures in three epilepsy patients.
items.summary: News report on the first clinical use of a chemogenetic strategy, in which engineered brain cells respond to a drug that dampens their activity. A team in China treated three patients with epilepsy. Only three patients were treated, so safety and benefit remain unproven.
items.title: Novel gene therapy lets drug dampen brain cell activity, reducing seizures.

items.hook: Aggressive blood pressure control in diabetes did not cut dementia risk, but slowed brain lesion growth.
items.hook_turn: but slowed brain lesion growth.

readout.label: Hazard ratio, dementia or MCI, intensive arm

items.summary: In a randomized trial of 12,434 Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes, targeting systolic pressure below 120 instead of 140 mm Hg did not significantly change dementia or mild cognitive impairment over a median of 3.8 years. In an MRI subset of 862 people, intensive treatment led to a smaller increase in white matter lesions. The trial was open label, and the MRI result comes from a small subset.
items.title: Effect of intensive blood pressure control on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes: prespecified analysis of secondary outcomes of BPROAD randomised controlled trial.

items.hook: A kelp suppresses asexual development when potential mates are present.
items.summary: Researchers compared gene expression and development in the kelp Laminaria pallida across sexual and asexual routes, plus two natural populations. Asexual reproduction came with endoreduplication and lower fitness, and it was rarely used in the wild. This suggests asexuality is a backup when mates are scarce; the work covers one species and two populations.
items.title: Life-cycle plasticity enables conditional asexual reproduction in a kelp.

items.hook: After learning alien sound categories, experts' auditory cortex favors the informative frequency band.
items.summary: Listeners who became expert at sorting synthetic alien sounds showed stronger fMRI responses to the frequency band that carried the identity cues, even when those cues stopped mattering. That bias matched the pattern seen when people deliberately attend to one tone band. The result comes from a small lab task with artificial sounds, so it may not carry over to speech or music.
items.title: Category learning drives cortical attentional gain to diagnostic dimensions of perceptual information.

items.hook: Mice detect calls in noise better when the noise has more structure, and PV neurons shape the effect.
items.summary: Mice trained to detect vocalizations hidden in sound textures did better when trials gave longer samples of the noise statistics and when frequencies were more strongly correlated. Auditory cortex recordings tracked this, and activating PV interneurons helped or hurt depending on the correlation level. The work is in mice with one task design, so links to human hearing are inferred.
items.title: Neural integration of acoustic statistics enables mice to detect acoustic targets in noise.

items.hook: Important genes are not shielded from mutation in E. coli or yeast; the claimed effects are tiny.
items.hook_turn: the claimed effects are tiny.
items.summary: A reanalysis of mutation accumulation data in wild-type E. coli and yeast found that genes with more abundant or essential proteins do not mutate less, and E. coli genes on the leading and lagging DNA strands mutate at similar rates. The authors controlled for covariates and used trinucleotide-matched simulations, and flagged an artefact in a standard statistical approach. Only a slight lower rate for highly transcribed E. coli genes remained, and it was not seen in yeast.
items.title: The importance of genes does not predict their mutation rate.

items.hook: CHIME finds a pulsar so bright that FAST could detect its pulses across the Local Group.
items.hook_turn: FAST could detect its pulses across the Local Group.

readout.label: Brightest pulse flux density, PSR J2108+5055

items.summary: Astronomers found PSR J2108+5055, a pulsar that emits sporadic bursts every 0.495 s, using the CHIME radio telescope. Its brightest pulse is far stronger than typical pulsar pulses, and the FAST telescope could detect such a pulse from the edge of the Local Group. The luminosity depends on a distance estimated from the dispersion measure, which carries real uncertainty.
items.title: Discovery of an Extremely Luminous Sporadic Radio Pulsar

items.hook: A 2 MeV bump and a roughly 40 MeV emission line show up in the brightest gamma-ray burst ever seen.
items.summary: Using two satellite instruments that did not saturate, the team rebuilt the 2 to 255 MeV spectrum of GRB 221009A over time. They report a spectral bump near 2 MeV and confirm a narrow line that drifts to lower energy as 1/t. They read this as hinting at a magnetically dominated jet with an empty center, but that is an interpretation of a single event.
items.title: Detection of 2 MeV Spectral Bump and ∼40 MeV Emission Line from GRB 221009A

items.hook: ALMA sees no circumplanetary dust around the proposed protoplanets in the AB Aurigae disk.
items.summary: Deep, sharp ALMA images of the young star AB Aurigae found no point source at the disputed protoplanet AB Aur b or at other candidates, and the gas there flows smoothly with the surrounding disk. Any circumplanetary dust must be sparse, small, optically thick or lacking large grains. A non-detection cannot rule out planets, only dust of the kind ALMA can see at this wavelength.
items.title: Searching for Circumplanetary Dust in the Cavity of the AB Aurigae Disk with ALMA
